analysis:
The changed files are CI test scripts only (.github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py, .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py). They touch no provider, coordinator or runtime code, so the TB-002 and TB-011 provider and attestation boundaries and the assets A-001..A-017 are not affected directly. No production code is in this batch.

The tests assert fail-closed behavior of the CI threat-review gate:
- Workload-policy call admission: no unplanned native Bedrock call, a hard emergency ceiling of 500, a ceiling of 12 for fixed probes, and bounds on invalid policy settings (test-threat-bedrock.py lines 302-378).
- No backup-provider fallback after unknown usage, truncation or refusal.
- A manual GitHub rerun (attempt > 1) hands off to a human with no paid work, and the report is not clean (test-threat-budget.py head lines 949-982).
- The scanner runtime is bounded to 60-3000 seconds.
- Large-scan completion via hierarchical integration still returns clean() only when integration is complete and there are no pending batches.
- Cross-file uncertainty now hands off to a human without an extra local rescan; the test expects [SONNET, SONNET]. Uncertainty still produces manual_review_reasons, so this relaxes redundant paid work rather than clearance.
- Membership and override gate tests: immutable org ID, active state, a separate membership token, and a per-attempt run ID so a stale report cannot clear.

I saw no test weakening that would let incomplete, stale or uncertain scans clear. The patch excerpts and test names show these tests are additive and strict. The actual implementations in threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_scan.py and merge_policy.py, and the production changes behind these tests, were not supplied, so I could not verify that the implementation matches the asserted behavior. Integration should check that the workload ceiling and rerun-disable logic are enforced in code and that removing the redundant local depth rescan does not lower gate coverage.
